title: The U.S. proposes a demilitarized zone in Donbas. Kyiv refuses to surrender territory. Putin insists it was Russia’s all along.
summary: The new U.S. peace plan calls for creating a demilitarized zone in Donbas, The Economist reported, citing Ukrainian officials. The plan also reportedly envisions Ukraine abandoning its bid to join NATO in exchange for an investment program and European Union membership. Russia would be offered eased sanctions and a partial restoration of ties with the West, possibly including a resumption of gas supplies to Europe and the restart of the Nord Stream pipelines. The Economist said these are only the outlines of the plan, and the details of the discussions remain unknown.

title: Norsk Redaktørforening gir Rustad ei formell åtvaring
summary: Styret i Norsk Redaktørforening har vedteke å gi Document-redaktør Hans Rustad ei formell åtvaring, skriv dei i ei pressemelding. Rustad har teke imot åtvaringa fredag. Grunngjevinga frå styret gjeld tre forhold: Manglande etterleving av grunnleggande journalistiske prinsipp, konkrete handlingar knytt til sjølvdømmeordninga og udokumenterte og sterke skuldingar mot andre redaktørstyrte medium. – Det er viktig for styret å understreke at målet med denne prosessen ikkje er eksklusjon. Styret ønsker vidare dialog og vil bidra konstruktivt, dersom Hans Rustad sjølv ønsker det, seier styreleiar Tora Bakke Håndlykken i Norsk Redaktørforening i pressemeldinga.

title: Bucharest-Ilfov among EU regions with highest GDP per capita growth in 2019-2024
summary: The Bucharest-Ilfov region is among the EU regions with the highest growth in GDP per capita in the 2019-2024 period, according to Eurostat , alongside regions in Ireland, Malta, and France. “The most robust GDP growth was recorded in the Irish capital region of Eastern and Midland, which also had the highest GDP per inhabitant in 2024, as GDP rose 38.0% between 2019 and 2024. The other 2 Irish regions also saw very high increases: Northern and Western up 36.4% (the 2nd highest in the EU) and Southern up 26.0% (6th highest),” Eurostat stated. Outside Ireland, the highest growth rates were recorded in the Bucharest-Ilfov region (33%), Malta (32.9%), and the French outermost region of Mayotte
